correctness.rationale: For a witness in a unit edge, a distance to a center is the minimum of distances via the two endpoints. If 2k≤r<2k+1, go to the nearer endpoint: centers reached via the farther endpoint have endpoint-distance at most k−1, so all centers are at distance at most k from the nearer endpoint. If 2k+1≤r<2k+2, all centers reached via either endpoint have integer endpoint-distance at most k and the midpoint witnesses them. Together with vertex witnesses this proves precisely the even/odd face rule and no intermediate changes for closed balls. An independent full enumeration gave face counts 12,30,109,423,2084,4095. Signed boundary Smith forms at the nontrivial stages give torsion-free homology and Betti vectors (12), (1,7), (1,3,1), (1,0,2,2), (1,0,0,2,1) in unreduced degrees. In the scale-two 1-cycle lattice of rank 32, the boundaries and included scale-one cycles span with Smith factors all 1, proving a split surjection onto Z^3 with kernel rank four. Independently the surjectivity follows by replacing a newly added distance-two edge by the other two sides of its closed-neighborhood triangle. Adjoining the included source cycle spaces to the target boundary spaces leaves ranks 86 for H_2(2)→H_2(3) and 293 for H_3(3)→H_3(4). Since the target groups are torsion-free the integral maps are zero. In particular the equal-rank map genuinely vanishes, and no zero-rank calculation over a finite field is used to infer that. The other maps are forced by the groups. The split map and single-scale groups give the stated integral interval sum without invoking a general interval theorem over Z.
residual_risks: No extension to the graph-vertex-only witness convention, a full continuum-centered nerve, or filtered homotopy type is asserted.
